Hi Asha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on token volumes, budget targets, and how bursts would be handled on our side.

Call recap (short):
- FinFlow MVP traffic estimate (from your product team): ~800M tokens/month steady-state across inference and embedding calls.
- Observed peak patterns: short spikes ~2.0x-2.5x steady for a few hours during batch report runs and marketing pushes; rare 4x spikes for under an hour.
- Primary ask: predictable unit economics and a workable overage policy that doesn't cause customer-facing outages.

Items we promised to clarify:
1) Unit economics goal: you mentioned a target band of ~$12–18 per 1M tokens — can you confirm if that target is for production (post-pilot) or for an initial pilot window?
2) Budget range: you indicated a monthly OPEX window of roughly $8k–$15k for month 1–3; please confirm whether that should include any reserved commitment or be purely on-hosted usage.
3) Burst behavior & rate limits: how long do you expect the 2–4x bursts to last in practice? We ask because our billing/overage options differ by burst duration and predictability.

What we recommend as next steps (proposed):
- You: confirm whether the $12–18/1M target is a firm procurement target or aspirational for later negotiations.
- Redwood: we will propose two concrete pricing options (hosted with smoothing vs reserved capacity) and a short addendum describing burst/overage rules.
- Tech pilot: agree on a 30-day pilot with telemetry that captures peak windows so we can tune batching and KV cache settings.

I attached the token-estimate workbook you shared (saved as FinFlow_MVP_token_estimates.xlsx) and flagged the rows we used.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if that helps iron out the pilot terms.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — quick answers and a couple of clarifications from our side.

1) $12–18/1M: that is our commercial target for production. For the pilot we can tolerate a higher effective rate if there is a clear path to the target within 60 days.
2) Budget: procurement is allocating an initial pilot budget of $10k/month. If we agree to a reserved commit that lowers the unit price substantially, we have flexibility to shift toward that mid-quarter.
3) Burst duration: typical marketing-driven bursts last 2–6 hours and happen ~2–3x/month; the 4x events are rare (<5/year) and usually tied to large customer demos.

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you outline what a pilot pricing path would look like that lands us at ~$12/1M within the first 60 days?
- How are short bursts (2–6 hours) billed vs. sustained overages? Do you have a smoothing/credit policy?
- What are the SLA implications if we hit a burst that exceeds our quota?

I attached our annotated token workbook — see sheet “prod_estimates”.

Thanks,

Neha/Priyom/Asha — thanks for the clear context. Below are two concrete commercial options and the overage mechanics we recommend for FinFlow’s profile. I’ve kept the math explicit so procurement can see the path to ~$12/1M.

Option 1 — Hosted (no long-term commit) + Pilot bridge:
- Pilot month rate: $20 per 1M tokens for month 1, 15% credit applied to invoice (effectively $17/1M) if pilot telemetry shows steady-state within +/-25% of estimates.
- Standard hosted rate post-pilot: $25 per 1M tokens.
- Burst smoothing for short spikes (<=6 hours): we apply a rolling 72-hour smoothing window and use token credits to absorb up to 20% of your monthly steady-state without immediate overage charge.
- Overage billing: short bursts inside smoothing window are covered by credits; sustained overages beyond smoothing are billed at 1.5x the standard rate for the overage bucket.

Option 2 — Reserved capacity (30-day commit) — recommended for predictable unit economics:
- Commit: 500M tokens/month reserved for $8,000/month (~$16/1M).
- Additional usage pricing (after reserved): tiered overage staircase
  - First 10% over reserved: $14 per 1M tokens
  - Next 20% over reserved: $18 per 1M tokens
  - Beyond that: $22 per 1M tokens
- True-up: monthly reconciled; we offer a 30-day period to transfer unused reserved capacity within the next month for credit.

Pilot-to-target path suggestion (to reach ~$12/1M):
- We can offer a short-term bridging credit for months 1–2 that effectively reduces the reserved blended unit cost toward $12/1M if FinFlow commits to a stepped reserve increase after month 2. Example: sign up for 500M reserved in month 2 and we apply a $6k credit spread across months 1–3 to reach an average ~$12/1M across that window. Exact numbers require procurement/legal sign-off.

SLA & operational notes:
- If quota is exceeded and smoothing window doesn’t cover the spike, we do not throttledge by default; instead we apply overage billing and notify both engineering teams. For customers with strict uptime requirements we recommend a fallback model (dedicated reserved pool) which includes an SLA for tail latency and availability.
- For rare extreme events (your 4x demos), we recommend a short-term burst reserve request — we can pre-authorize capacity for specific dates and provide a one-off quote.

Next steps I propose:
1) Neha: share both Option 1 and Option 2 with Procurement (Asha) and confirm which path they want detailed into an SOW.
2) Priyom: please attach the one-page addendum on smoothing & overage; I leaned on your previous draft and added the tiers above.
3) If Asha agrees, we will prepare a two-page pilot commercial that includes the bridging credit example and a simple amendment for the reserved commit.

Asha — happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk procurement through the staircase math if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Director | Redwood Inference
